At request of Sri.Sathisha.T, learned counsel for the appellants who appears through video conference and
Sri.Mallikarjuna Reddy who represents Sri.Pradeep.B, learned counsel on record for respondent No.2 and who appears before this Court physically, the matter is taken up for final hearing and disposal.

2. Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Tumakuru in MVC No.615/2023 dated 27.11.2024.
This is a claimants' appeal.

3. The only point that is projected by the learned counsel for the appellants is in respect of the amount that is awarded as compensation towards loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Learned counsel who represents respondent No.2 seeks to dispose of the matter in accordance with law.
NC: 2025:KHC:35084 HC-KAR 4.

It is not in dispute that the first appellant is the husband, second appellant is the major son and the third appellant is the major daughter of the deceased Nagarathnamma who died in a road traffic accident.
The accident occurred in the year 2023.

Therefore, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the first appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- under the head 'loss of spousal consortium'.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant Nos.2 and 3 being the children of the deceased are also entitled to Rs.44,000/- under the head 'loss of parental consortium'.
The appellants are also entitled to a sum of Rs.16,500/- towards 'funeral expenses' and Rs.16,500/- towards 'loss of estate'.
Thus the total sum which the appellants are entitled to towards loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is Rs.1,21,000/-.
However, the Tribunal awarded sum of Rs.70,000/- only in toto under the said heads.
Thus the NC: 2025:KHC:35084 HC-KAR additional amount which the appellants are entitled to is Rs.51,000/-.

5. Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Tumakuru through orders in MVC No.615/2023 dated 27.11.2024 is enhanced by Rs.51,000/-.
